title: The Town Keeper
statement: A village has n people, numbered 0 to n − 1. Each pair [a, b] in `trust` means person a trusts person b; trust goes one way only. The village has a keeper if exactly one person is trusted by every other person and trusts nobody. Return the keeper's number, or −1 if there is no keeper.
constraints: trust[i] = [a, b] with a != b, and no pair repeats

answerKey.pattern: In-degree and out-degree in a directed graph
keyPoints: Each pair [a, b] is a directed edge from a to b
Count, for every person, the arrows in (trusted by) and the arrows out (trusts)
The keeper has n − 1 arrows in and 0 arrows out
A single array of (in − out) equal to n − 1 also works
edgeCases: n = 1 with no trust: person 0 is the keeper
Everyone trusts the candidate, but the candidate trusts someone
acceptableSlowerApproaches: For each person, scan all pairs to check the two conditions: O(V · E)

hints: Draw each pair as an arrow. What do the keeper's arrows look like?
The keeper has an arrow from every other person (n − 1 in) and no arrows going out.
Count arrows in and out for everyone in one pass, then look for in = n − 1 and out = 0.
